findings.summary: AMP is an open-source HTML framework designed to accelerate mobile web page loading. It achieves speed through a restricted HTML subset that disallows synchronous JavaScript and certain CSS patterns, and it enforces resource loading constraints. Content can be cached by third-party CDNs, such as Cloudflare and Bing, enabling faster serving. The project transitioned to open governance under the OpenJS Foundation in 2019. While initially promoted as "Accelerated Mobile Pages," the acronym was later dropped, though the framework continues to support many device types with responsive design features.

mechanisms.title: HTML Restriction and Validation
mechanisms.explanation: AMP enforces a strict subset of HTML that disallows synchronous JavaScript and certain blocking CSS patterns, ensuring resources can be identified and loaded efficiently without render-blocking delays.

mechanisms.title: CDN Caching and Pre-rendering
mechanisms.explanation: AMP content may be cached by Content Delivery Networks, which allows pages to be served more quickly to users, often with pre-rendering capabilities that reduce perceived load time.
